messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: ALERT fired: gpu_node_drain_loop_high_ecc_count (severity=page)
IncidentBot: nodes: gpu-cluster-eu-3a-[n1,n2], 3x ECC events in 10m -> auto-drain triggered
Priya (oncall): Paging, I'm on it. Seeing repeated ECC counters + kernel nvlink resets on n1. Starting triage.
Priya (oncall): Quick note: traffic routing has already pushed ~30% of inference traffic off cluster to fallback-hosts per routing policy.
Luca (sre): Looking at telemetry — VRAM pressure spiked before ECCs on n1, but on n2/n3 ECCs seem independent. Could be thermal + firmware flakiness.
Aisha (runtime): Rolling logs from the runtime:
```
2026-03-14T21:08:12Z [node-n1] ECC: device 0000:3b:00.0 error count +1
2026-03-14T21:08:15Z [runtime] kv-cache flush due to mem-pressure seq=842
2026-03-14T21:09:01Z [node-n1] nvlink reset triggered
```
Priya (oncall): I've muted the repeated non-actionable ECC-count alert for this cluster for 30m to reduce noise `/alert mute gpu_node_ecc_count cluster=gpu-cluster-eu-3a duration=30m`
Luca (sre): +1 on muting. We still need a durable fix: either tune threshold/burst window or move to delta-based alerting. Current rule is too sensitive to short-lived spikes.
Jordan (prod-eng): Customer impact? Any 5xx/latency spikes we should notify SRE-Customer?
Priya (oncall): Early metrics: 503s spiked from 0.02% -> 0.45% for hosted API in eu region for ~12m. Dedicated customers saw transient queueing and increased per-request latency (~150ms p50 -> 320ms p50). No data loss.
Aisha (runtime): Mitigations applied: 1) drained node-n1, 2) forced model-fanout to fallback variants for small requests, 3) increased dedicated pool burst by 2 instances. That reduced errors to baseline.
Luca (sre): For follow-up: propose changing these alerts:
- ECC alert: require 3 errors in 10m AND node ECC rate > 0.5/min for 15m (reduce sensitivity).
- VRAM pressure: switch from instant >90% to 90% sustained over 5m for >5 pods.
- Node drain flapping: add a dedupe window (snooze) so we don't auto-drain again within 20m of previous drain unless error persists.
Priya (oncall): I sketched a Prometheus alert rule patch and pushed to staging repo: `git commit -m "tune gpu ECC and vram alerts"`
Aisha (runtime): Can we also add a Grafana panel that correlates ECC count + VRAM + fan RPM + node temp in one row per node? That'll make post-incident triage faster.
Luca (sre): Agreed. I created a temporary dashboard and saved as draft: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/kh2yGxgk/gpu-health-eu?orgId=1 (draft). We'll promote after review.
Jordan (prod-eng): For customer comms: prepare an internal blurb: impact window, affected region, mitigation steps, customers possibly affected (Dedicated capacity owners). I'll sync with growth on whether we need outbound.
Priya (oncall): Action items captured:
- Luca: push alert rule changes to alertmanager and run canary in eu staging (ETA: 6h).
- Aisha: add combined GPU health dashboard, include fan RPM and nvlink resets (ETA: 8h).
- Priya: write initial incident summary + customer impact numbers and hand off to Jordan for comms (ETA: 2h).
- Jordan: evaluate whether any Dedicated contracts require formal notice (ETA: 4h).
Luca (sre): Also adding a metric aggregation: report ECC events per-device per-hour instead of raw counters. That should reduce false positive on short bursts.
Priya (oncall): Handoff: my shift ends in ~30m. Next oncall is Luca — Luca, you're the primary after the handoff, I'll DM any live links.
Luca (sre): Taking handoff. If anything spikes again, escalate to eng-sre@pager and call infra-oncall.
IncidentBot: Handoff recorded: from Priya (oncall) -> Luca (sre) at 1890010100
Priya (oncall): Quick note for postmortem: include sequence diagrams of routing fallback + which models were promoted. We want to ensure rollback steps are documented.
Aisha (runtime): Also check firmware revision of affected nodes; I'll file a ticket with infra for firmware roll-forward if we see pattern.
Jordan (prod-eng): Thanks team. I'll wait for Priya's summary, then draft the external/internal communications.
Priya (oncall): Closing here — monitoring will be relaxed but new rules will go through testing. Filing follow-up PRs and a 1-hour postmortem meeting tomorrow 10:00 UTC. :calendar:
Luca (sre): Noted. We'll also add a short runbook entry: conditions to avoid auto-drain during transient ECC bursts and how to manually force drain when persistent.
IncidentBot: Incident status -> acknowledged -> under-mitigation -> follow-up required
